added_lemmas.justification: This mandated boundary corollary converts the exact aggregation bridge and the realizable positive cycle loss into a counterexample for the published individual-imputation procedure without exporting an efficiency bound across experiments.
added_lemmas.gap: Moreau--Kastler (2025, printed pp. 15 and 20--23, equations (3.1), (3.2), (3.13), (3.14), and (3.19)) defines the individual fixed-effects specification and imputation ratio but does not give a positive-cycle semiparametric nonuniversality result.
added_lemmas.consumer: Users of the Nagengast--Yotov regional-trade-agreement and Menkhoff--Miethe treaty and bank-deposit applications obtain a rigorous warning that exact aggregation does not make the published PPML estimator universally efficient.

prose_updates.tldr: At fixed \(T\), with a never-treated cohort, positive multiplicative untreated means, independent cohorts, arbitrary within-unit dependence, and finite fourth moments, one weighted tangent restriction arises from each untreated graph cycle. Bounded score truncation followed by an exact mean correction proves tangent completeness in the explicitly mean-differentiable experiment. The canonical gradient removes the covariance projection of the cohort-mean PPML influence onto the \(q\) cycle directions; a feasible correction attains the bound and supports pointwise Wald inference. The cohort-mean PPML estimator is efficient for every bounded legal covariance law exactly when \(q=0\); for \(q>0\), exactly \(q\) primitive balances characterize its exceptional efficient laws, and a bounded strictly positive fixed-support family has exact loss \(\Gamma>0\). On the balanced equal-weight, no-covariate, no-offset intersection with Moreau--Kastler, the individual and cohort-mean point estimators coincide, so the same family and the regular cycle-corrected competitor prove that the published individual estimator is not universally efficient when \(q>0\). This transfer is one-way: it gives neither the richer individual-level efficiency bound nor a \(q=0\) efficiency conclusion there. The regularized frontier for growing \(T\) and \(q\) remains open at \(\mathrm{oeq{:}growing\text{-}cycle\text{-}frontier}\).

project_justification.gap: Moreau--Kastler (2025, printed pp. 15 and 20--23, equations (3.1), (3.2), (3.13), (3.14), and (3.19)) gives an individual fixed-effects PPML specification, imputation ratio, and inference procedure; it does not characterize universal semiparametric efficiency by untreated-cycle topology. Wooldridge (2023) studies a richer individual-level nonlinear imputation framework, while existing efficient staggered-DiD results are additive and rank-one completion results do not classify covariance-sensitive efficiency for proportional treatment on the treated.
project_justification.niche: In the fixed-\(T\) cohort-mean experiment, positive rank-one means make graph cycles both the complete tangent restrictions and the available covariance-sensitive precision directions. The exact aggregation boundary then embeds a balanced equal-weight, no-covariate, no-offset subclass of the published Moreau--Kastler specification, allowing a strict \(q>0\) nonuniversality conclusion without claiming that the cohort-mean bound governs the unrestricted individual-level experiment.
project_justification.fill: The project proves weighted-cycle tangent completeness using bounded score truncation plus exact mean correction, derives the canonical gradient and the cohort-mean PPML influence, constructs an attaining covariance-weighted cycle correction, characterizes the efficient covariance laws by \(q\) independent primitive balances, and certifies exact positive quadratic loss on an open realizable bounded-law family. The aggregation bridge and positive-cycle corollary show that the published individual estimator inherits strict inefficiency on their precise intersection. The growing-\(T\), growing-\(q\) regularized frontier remains open at \(\mathrm{oeq{:}growing\text{-}cycle\text{-}frontier}\).

prose_updates.related_work: Moreau--Kastler (2025, printed pp. 15 and 20--23, equations (3.1), (3.2), (3.13), (3.14), and (3.19); \url{https://taxobservatory.world/www-site/uploads/2025/05/WP31_-Proportional-Treatment-Effects-in-Staggered-Settings.pdf}) specifies individual fixed effects and time effects, imputes individual untreated counterfactuals, aggregates a treated observed-to-predicted ratio, and develops inference. The aggregation proposition proves point-estimator coincidence with the cohort-mean rank-one PPML procedure only for balanced panels with equal observation weights, no covariates or offsets, and exact equality between target and sample cohort shares. Point-estimator coincidence alone does not transfer efficiency bounds. The positive-cycle corollary instead uses the regular cohort-mean cycle correction as a strictly better competitor on that intersection, which is sufficient to refute universal efficiency for \(q>0\), but it does not assert that \(V^{\star}\) is the unrestricted individual-level bound or that \(q=0\) yields individual-level efficiency. Wooldridge (2023, Sections 2--3) studies fully interacted individual-level nonlinear imputation and does not supply the cohort-mean cycle frontier. Ciani and Fisher (2019, printed page 7, Section 3.1 and Appendix B) note and simulate possible PPML inefficiency; the present fixed-horizon result supplies necessity, sufficiency, exact codimension, and a realizable strict-loss neighborhood. Kir\'aly, Theran, and Tomioka (2015, Theorem 34 and Remark 35) identify even cycles as rank-one matrix circuits. Chamberlain (1987) and Newey (1990) provide general efficiency and score tools, while the support-preserving bounded-score truncation and exact mean correction are proved here for this nonnegative panel. Roth and Sant'Anna (2023), Borusyak, Jaravel, and Spiess (2024), and Chen, Sant'Anna, and Xie (2025) concern covariance-aware additive staggered designs rather than this proportional ratio. Nagengast--Yotov and Menkhoff--Miethe are motivating applications; their richer dependence and fixed effects remain outside the benchmark. No theorem here resolves the growing-\(T\), growing-\(q\) regularized problem posed at \(\mathrm{oeq{:}growing\text{-}cycle\text{-}frontier}\).
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Because \(\infty\in C\) and the panel is fully observed, \(q=\sum_{g<\infty}(g-2)\); the topology theorem does not claim arbitrary missing-panel graph generality. There is no positive loss bound uniform over all inefficient laws because \(\Gamma(x)\to0\) as \(x\to0\). Singular covariance blocks, zero mean cells, random cohort shares, growing \(T\), unbalanced panels, and dyadic shared-country dependence are outside the formal model. The finite-fourth-moment tangent result is pointwise for the explicitly mean-differentiable differentiable-in-quadratic-mean experiment and uses bounded support-preserving submodels constructed by truncation and exact mean correction; it does not classify tail-escaping paths for which score-moment differentiation fails. The Moreau--Kastler transfer is confined to the balanced equal-weight, no-covariate, no-offset intersection with exact shares: strict \(q>0\) loss transfers because a regular lower-variance competitor restricts to that intersection, but neither the cohort-mean bound nor the \(q=0\) efficiency conclusion transfers to the unrestricted richer individual-level experiment.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The fixed-horizon contributions are PTT-specific weighted-cycle completeness, constructive tangent equality for the explicitly mean-differentiable finite-fourth-moment experiment, the exact rank-\(q\) primitive covariance map, the acyclic universal-efficiency equivalence for the cohort-mean estimator, and a bounded strictly positive family with exact quadratic loss and an ambient positive-radius strict-loss neighborhood. The feasible covariance-weighted correction attains the cohort-mean bound and supports pointwise inference. Exact equality with Moreau--Kastler's individual estimator is confined to balanced equal-weight panels without covariates or offsets and with target shares equal to sample shares. On that intersection, the \(q>0\) family yields a strictly better regular competitor and therefore refutes universal efficiency of the published individual estimator; no unrestricted individual-level bound and no \(q=0\) individual-level efficiency result is claimed. Canonical projection algebra and routine sandwich consistency are supporting machinery. The growing-horizon, growing-cycle-rank regularized frontier remains open at \(\mathrm{oeq{:}growing\text{-}cycle\text{-}frontier}\).

statement_notes.justification: The proposition proves a deterministic point-estimator identity under exact aggregation conditions; that identity is needed for the positive-cycle counterexample but, by itself, transfers no semiparametric efficiency bound.
statement_notes.gap: Moreau--Kastler (2025, printed pp. 15 and 20--23, equations (3.1), (3.2), (3.13), (3.14), and (3.19)) presents the individual specification and imputation estimator but not the profiling identity with the cohort-mean rank-one score or any cross-experiment efficiency transfer.
statement_notes.consumer: Applied users can test whether their implementation lies on the exact aggregation boundary and can avoid treating point-estimator coincidence as evidence that two statistical experiments share an efficiency bound.
